optionReasons.saa-ini-287:option:1: Transfer between AZs DENTRO of the same region is also charged (~US$ 0,01/GB) — not only between regions.
optionReasons.saa-ini-287:option:2: Not all traffic is free — Internet exit and traffic between AZs/Regions is charged.
optionReasons.saa-ini-287:option:3: There is no universal single rate — entry is free and prices vary by route and region.

finalJustifications: Because the rule is: free entry; Internet access charged by GB; same free AZ for many pairs; between AZs ~US$ 0,01/GB; between regions charged as a way out.
Because the AWS charges the same rate per GB for any data handling, whether in, out or traffic between internal services.
Because only uploads are charged at AWS — the input rate exists to discourage mass data migration to the cloud.
Because traffic between AZs is always free because it is part of the same region — the collection starts only between different regions.

optionReasons.saa-ini-054:option:1: Restoring an old snapshot would lose the replicated transactions since then — the replica is much more up-to-date (better RPO).
optionReasons.saa-ini-054:option:2: ElastiCache is cache in memory — no replica conversion RDS in cache cluster.
optionReasons.saa-ini-054:option:3: The RDS DO NOT fail automatic between regions — cross-region replica requires manual promotion (or orchestrated by you)).

finalJustifications: Because a cross-region replica read can be PROMOVIDA the independent instance of reading and writing — continuous replication (good RPO) + rapid promotion (good) RTO).
Because the promotion converts the replica into a consistent snapshot, which is restored in São Paulo as soon as the region recovers.
Because the cross-region replica already accepts written normally — just point out the DNS application to the Ohio endpoint.
Because RDS detects the regional disaster and promotes the replication automatically, without any action of the company's operations team.

optionReasons.saa-ini-055:option:0: Disable the Auto Scaling eliminates elasticity and self-recovery — treats the symptom by sabotaging architecture.
optionReasons.saa-ini-055:option:1: There are always users connected in real applications — and the scale-in needs to happen when demand falls, not on schedule.
optionReasons.saa-ini-055:option:2: More memory does not resolve: when the instance is removed, local sessions continue to be lost.

finalJustifications: Why state authorities do not keep local status: with sessions in ElastiCache/DynamoDB, any instance attends any user and removals do not lose carts.
Because ElastiCache signals to Auto Scaling which instances have active users, preventing removal while there are open sessions.
Because moving the sessions out makes the instances immune to hardware failures, since the hypervisor realocates the preserved memory.
Because DynamoDB synchronizes memory RAM among all the instances of the group, replicating the carts to the surviving nodes.

optionReasons.saa-ini-063:option:0: The AWS Backup centralizes backups — no memory queries.
optionReasons.saa-ini-063:option:1: The S3 is storage of durable objects — latency is milliseconds, not the RAM of microseconds requested.
optionReasons.saa-ini-063:option:2: The Redshift is data warehouse for mass analysis — is not ultra-fast access cache layer.

finalJustifications: Because ElastiCache keeps the results frequent in memory (Redis/Memcached), serving in microseconds and relieving the bench — cache-aside pattern.
Because ElastiCache completely replaces the relational bank in reading loads, taking on headline appointments.
Because ElastiCache replicates the entire bank to the RAM automatically, keeping a mirrored copy always updated.
Because ElastiCache schedules the consultation to the bank once a day and serves the frozen result in the other requests.

optionReasons.saa-ini-069:option:0: There is no automatic wheel between main and replicas — promotion only occurs in failover/manual promotion.
optionReasons.saa-ini-069:option:2: Read replicas of RDS accept only LEITURAS — the writings remain exclusive of the main.
optionReasons.saa-ini-069:option:3: Replicas contain a complete copy of the data, not just the indexes.

finalJustifications: Because the Read Replicas receive ASSIGNRONA replication from the main and attend reading queries, distributing the load and releasing the main for writing.
Because replicas use synchronous replication, ensuring that each reading sees exactly the same data from the main instance.
Because the replicas assume the writings when the main one is busy, returning the changes in the next synchronization.
Because RDS redirects the readings to the replicas automatically, without the application having to change the connection string.

finalJustifications: Because DAX is the cache in memory NATIVO and compatible with the API of the DynamoDB: Just point the client to the cluster and the readings fall to microseconds.
Because DAX rewrites the game's wants to use global secondary indexes, the fastest way to scoreboards.

optionReasons.saa-ini-071:option:0: It is the closest because it is the other mode of real capacity of the DynamoDB, the same concept of the right answer — but low fixed values would cause throttling in the peaks of millions of requests and still require manual capacity management that the question asks to avoid.
optionReasons.saa-ini-071:option:1: Reserved Capacity presupposes PREVIOUS burden for years — the opposite of the scenario.
optionReasons.saa-ini-071:option:3: High fixed values waste money in long periods of low traffic.

finalJustifications: Because on-demand mode instantly scales with real traffic and charges for effective requisition — ideal for unpredictable loads and new apps without history.
Because on-demand is always cheaper than the provided mode, in any usage pattern — it is the standard recommended by AWS.
Because the on-demand reserve fixed capacity in each AZ of the region, absorbing any peak without risk of throttling in the writings.
Because on-demand eliminates the limit of 400 KB per item from DynamoDB, common requirement for applications with unpredictable traffic.

optionReasons.saa-ini-077:option:1: It seems plausible because the DynamoDB also delivers very high throughput in a managed way — but it is NoSQL: migrating would require rewriting the data model and all queries, breaking the MySQL compatibility that the issue requires; Aurora gives the performance gain while keeping the wants.

finalJustifications: Because Aurora MySQL uses distributed storage redesigned to the cloud, delivering up 5x the standard MySQL throughput with full match.
Because Aurora converts MySQL queries to proprietary binary format, run by faster optimizer.
Because Aurora executes MySQL in instances with GPU, parallelizing the heavy queries of the catalog in graphic hardware.
Because Aurora eliminates the need for indexes: distributed storage locates any line in constant time.
